title: How to Export SentinelOne Logs
content_md: SentinelOne keeps three kinds of data worth exporting: endpoint telemetry, threats, and activities (the audit trail of what users and agents did in the console). Telemetry lives in Singularity Data Lake and has its own guide. Threats and activities come out of the management API (https:// .sentinelone.net/web/api/v2.1) with an ApiToken header, as JSON, page by page with a cursor. When something goes wrong on a SentinelOne-protected network, the activity log often answers the uncomfortable questions. Who disabled that agent? Who added that exclusion? Who marked the threat as benign? Prime Core has 14,741 detection rules for SentinelOne, mapped to 644 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get the data out, sanitize it, and investigate it for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start An API token. Create a service user (or use your own user) with view rights at the account or site that holds the data, and generate its API token. Tokens expire; note when. Your console URL. It’s the hostname you log in to, for example https://usea1-example.sentinelone.net. Export activities and threats S1="https://usea1-example.sentinelone.net/web/api/v2.1" H="Authorization: ApiToken $S1_API_TOKEN" URL="$S1/activities?createdAt__gte=2026-10-19T00:00:00Z&createdAt__lt=2026-10-20T00:00:00Z&limit=1000" : > s1_activities_1019.jsonl NEXT="" while :; do RESP=$(curl -sS -H "$H" "${URL}${NEXT:+&cursor=$NEXT}") echo "$RESP" | jq -c '.data[]' >> s1_activities_1019.jsonl NEXT=$(echo "$RESP"
